video_title: Chandler Parsons and Mark Cuban BULLIED the Houston Rockets to get his Dallas contract 💀

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Chandler Parsons on leaving Houston as a restricted free agent
quotes.excerpt: There's agents that get you paid, Dan Fegan gets you overpaid.

text_blocks.speaker: Zach Randolph
text_blocks.text: Was it a bittersweet moment leaving Houston?

text_blocks.speaker: Chandler Parsons
text_blocks.text: Yes, that was a unique deal where I was a restricted free agent and I had a team option in my third in my fourth year for the Rockets, which ended up helping me because I remember I was overplaying my contract and I exceeded all expectations. By the time my fourth year came up, I was playing 40 minutes a night and I was a starter. So it was like, okay, how do we extend this guy? And I remember this is when then I hired Dan Fegan, who rest in peace, he was a great goat of, yeah, there's agents that get you paid, Dan Fegan gets you overpaid.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Houston Rockets refusing to match Chandler Parsons' max contract offer
quotes.excerpt: This was the biggest raise in the history of the NBA too back in the day.
quotes.quote: They didn't pick it up. And so they didn't pick it up and that summer I played great, I became a restricted free agent. And that's when Mark Cuban comes in, he offers me a max deal, this other I think Orlando offered me a big deal. And it was restricted and he put in a no-trade, I had the craziest kickers and a player option in my year. There was incentives in my contract where they were very player friendly to where I had the option to get out of the contract a year early. I had the option to get even more of a raise if I get traded. There was a bunch of stuff in there to where literally Houston didn't match it and we did this to strong arm them. I wanted to go back. And then Mark offered me the three-year deal in Dallas and they get like three days or whatever to match the contract if you're a restricted free agent versus an unrestricted free agent. And they didn't match it. So it is bittersweet because I never wanted to leave Houston. I loved Houston. I loved playing for Kevin McHale. I loved playing with James and Dwight and we only had that one season together where Damian Lillard hit the shot and we got eliminated Game 6. But like yeah, but now this was the biggest raise in the history of the NBA too back in the day. I went from making $700 grand to $15 million a year.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Chandler Parsons' wild first meeting with Dallas Mavericks owner Mark Cuban
quotes.excerpt: We literally went to my apartment afterwards. Picture a room like this and we just wrestled right there.
quotes.quote: I met Mark Cuban All-Star weekend in Houston where we went to a party, we got so fucked up. After we went back to my place and everyone surrounded us and we wrestled. This is while I was on the Rockets. We literally went to my apartment afterwards. Picture a room like this and we just wrestled right there. And that's how I met him. And I just became cool with that and obviously I was always interested in business and he was the shark, he was the man, he was this famous cool owner. He liked the same stuff I liked to do in the offseason, he was my guy. And so I developed this relationship with him early. He was very close with Dan Fegan, my agent at the time. So yeah, I went in there not only leaving bittersweet to leave Houston, but now I'm going to play for Dallas, who my boy is the owner, my hero, role model, Dirk is my teammate.

quotes.speaker: Chandler Parsons
quotes.summary_phrase: Chandler Parsons on Dallas Mavericks being the perfect fit for his game
quotes.excerpt: It was the perfect storm going in there, close to Houston, it's right there in the same state.
quotes.quote: 100%. Rick Carlisle, they had just won the chip in 2011 and he's a great coach. You see all these numbers offensively, a lot of pick and roll, a lot of threes. And it's exactly like was my game. So it was the perfect storm going in there, close to Houston, it's right there in the same state, no state taxes. There was a lot of perks going there and again, now you got Mark Cuban on your side too, who's your boy, who'll take care of you post-career, business, etc. So it was awesome and I was obsessed with Dirk. I remember I have a yearbook picture wearing Dirk's jersey and then here we go fast forward 15 years later, he's my teammate. That was awesome and those were great times. We had good team, good teams too and that's when the injuries started happening. That's where I had my first knee surgery and kind of domino effect from there, but those it was a three-year deal, I ended up only playing there for two years, but those two years were great relationships.
